title: feat!: drop Python 3.10 and require numpy 2, pandas 2.2, pyarrow 26
body:
## What

Closes #394. Mend flags pyarrow 25.0.1 in `requirements.txt` for CVE-2026-92287 (CVSS 8.1). Modernises the support matrix at the same time: Python 3.11 to 3.14, pandas 2, numpy 2.

## Changes

- `requirements.txt`: pyarrow 25.0.1 to 26.0.1, single line. A full `uv pip compile --upgrade-package pyarrow` also re-resolves numpy, pandas and polars, not worth the noise.
- `pyproject.toml`: `requires-python >=3.11.0`, classifiers 3.11 to 3.14, floors `pandas>=2.2.0`, `numpy>=2.0.0`, `pyarrow>=26.0.1`, ruff `target-version` py311, pyarrow and polars added to the edgetest upgrade list so the lock stops rotting.
- `tox.ini`: replaced the pandas15 and pandas20 legs (both only existed to hold numpy below 2) with a `mindeps` floor leg, added `pandas31`, spread the legs across 3.11 to 3.14, and removed `ignore_outcome` from `pandas30`.
- Workflows: publish and docs 3.10 to 3.12, lint 3.10 to 3.11, matrix 3.11 to 3.14.
- `tests/test_utility.py`: `datetime.timezone.utc` to `datetime.UTC` (UP017, newly enforced at py311).
- `README.rst`: supported range 3.11 to 3.14.

## Why

Mend scans the lock, not pyproject, but the old floors still advertised pyarrow 10 and numpy 1.22 as supported. pyarrow 26 declares no dependency metadata on PyPI, so pip will happily pair it with numpy 1.x and then fail at import with `pyarrow requires NumPy 2.0 or newer`. Since `import pyarrow` is top level in `utility.py` that makes locopy unimportable, so the pyarrow floor has to move together with numpy and pandas. pandas 2.0 predates numpy 2 support and fails with a binary incompatibility, hence the 2.2.0 floor.

The pandas30 leg had `ignore_outcome = true` on the stated basis that snowflake-connector-python caps pandas below 3.0. That cap does not exist in 5.2.0 (`pandas>=1.0.0`, `>=2.1.2` on 3.13+, `>=3.0.0` on 3.15+), so the leg was reporting without gating. It gates now.

The CVE itself is unreachable in locopy. pyarrow is used only for `pa.types.is_*` predicates in `utility.py`; locopy never reads Parquet through pyarrow and never configures a `KmsClient`. This clears the finding and stops the floors advertising vulnerable resolutions, it does not close an exploitable hole.

## Tests

`pytest tests -m "not integration"` against the new floors, 212 passed / 24 deselected on each:

| python | numpy | pandas | pyarrow |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 3.11 | 2.4.6 | 3.1.1 | 26.0.1 |
| 3.12 | 2.5.4 | 3.1.1 | 26.0.1 |
| 3.13 | 2.5.4 | 3.1.1 | 26.0.1 |
| 3.14 | 2.5.4 | 3.1.1 | 26.0.1 |

Full `tox` run, 4/4 OK in 85s: mindeps (3.11, pandas 2.2.3 + numpy 2.0.2 + pyarrow 26.0.1), pandas23 (3.12), pandas30 (3.13), pandas31 (3.14). `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean at py311. Wheel METADATA confirms `Requires-Python: >=3.11.0` with the three new floors.

title: Redact AWS credential values from SQL written to the log
body:
This masks the AWS secret access key and session token in the SQL that execute writes to the log. The COPY and UNLOAD statements include a credentials clause and the SQL is logged at info level by default so the values can reach the logs. The change adds a small redaction helper and applies it on the log line only. Behaviour is otherwise unchanged.

For full detail I can be reached at partnerships@Quantova.org.

[![CLA assistant check](https://cla-assistant.io/pull/badge/signed)](https://cla-assistant.io/capitalone/locopy?pullRequest=399)
All committers have signed the CLA.
@quantova-inc Thanks for the PR. If you have a moment to sign the CLA that would be greatly appreciated.

Could you add a test for the redaction? Something like this in `tests/test_database.py` would do it (it needs `import logging` at the top):

```python
@pytest.mark.parametrize("dbapi", DBAPIS)
def test_execute_redacts_credentials_in_log(credentials, dbapi, caplog):
    sql = (
        "COPY tbl FROM 's3://bucket/file.csv' CREDENTIALS "
        "'aws_access_key_id=AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE;"
        "aws_secret_access_key=wJalrXUtnFEMI;token=SESSIONTOKEN' CSV;"
    )
    with (
        mock.patch(dbapi.__name__ + ".connect"),
        Database(dbapi=dbapi, **credentials) as test,
        caplog.at_level(logging.INFO, logger="locopy.database"),
    ):
        test.execute(sql)
    assert "wJalrXUtnFEMI" not in caplog.text
    assert "SESSIONTOKEN" not in caplog.text
    assert test.cursor.execute.call_args[0][0] == sql
```

Done. I added that test in tests/test_database.py and pushed it.

I ran it both ways to be sure.

With the fix the test passes for all four dbapis.

Without the fix the log line puts the raw sql back and all four fail. The log then shows the secret in the clear with aws_secret_access_key=wJalrXUtnFEMI and token=SESSIONTOKEN. That is the leak this change closes.

The test also checks the sql handed to the cursor is unchanged so only the log is redacted and the query still runs as before.

Thanks for the review.

title: fix: support pandas 3.0 dtype changes, add tox matrix for pandas versions
body:
### Summary

- pandas 3.0 changed how text and datetime columns are typed internally (str dtype instead of object, plus non-nanosecond
datetime64 resolutions). find_column_type_pandas only checked for the old forms, so date/timestamp columns were silently mistyped as varchar on pandas 3.0, this is what broke edgetest.
- Fixed by switching to pandas' own is_string_dtype/is_datetime64_any_dtype checks, which cover both the old and new forms and are stable back to pandas 1.5.
- Widened the pandas pin to <=3.0.5 now that the code handles it correctly.
- Added tox.ini with a matrix across pandas 1.5, 2.0, 2.2, 2.3, and 3.0, wired into CI, so a future pandas release breaking
this again gets caught immediately instead of waiting on the weekly edgetest run. The 3.0 env is allowed to fail since
snowflake-connector-python itself still caps at pandas<3.0.

### Test plan

- [x] pytest -m "not integration" passes (94 passed)
- [x] Verified against pandas 3.0's dtype behavior directly (string dtype, datetime64 resolutions)
- [x] Ran tox end-to-end to confirm env creation, install ordering, and test execution work

title: Datetime and other temporal datatypes parsing
body:
This PR fixes two bugs.

1. For columns that only includes `date` (not `datetime`) eg. "2023-01-08", polars support for `find_column_type` was parsing it incorrectly as `timestamp`, which leads to mismatch in sql format. This is now fixed, and added support for `time` (%H:%M:%S) as well.
2. When copying from internal stage parquet files to table or vice versa, if there are columns stored as `datetime` or any of the temporal datatype, snowflake will not parse it properly as the time is stored as epoch time in parquet files. One of the fix is to allow users to specify a [file format](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/sql/create-file-format#examples) where `USE_LOGICAL_TYPE = TRUE;` to allow proper transfer. More information [here](https://community.snowflake.com/s/article/How-to-load-logical-type-TIMESTAMP-data-from-Parquet-files-into-Snowflake).
